blocks.text: Act One: A Century in the Making is a forthcoming 700-page publication and accompanying exhibition bringing together more than 100 internationally renowned photographers alongside leading scholars, journalists, historians, and public intellectuals to examine the defining forces, conflicts, transformations, and human realities of the first quarter of the 21st century.

links.text: Act One: A Century in the Making

blocks.text: Published by Other Side Editions , a New York-based non-profit publishing house, Act One explores major themes shaping contemporary life — including climate change, war and conflict, race in America, democracy, globalization, public health, technology, deindustrialization, and human rights — through a combination of photographic narratives and original critical essays.

The project features work by acclaimed photographers including Albert Watson, Andres Serrano, Platon, Martin Schoeller, Eugene Richards, Nick Brandt, Andrea Bruce, Christopher Morris, Peter van Agtmael, Darcy Padilla, David Maisel, Mandy Barker, Andrew Moore, David Burnett, Bryan Schutmaat, Shadi Ghadirian and many others working across documentary photography, portraiture, conceptual practice, reportage, and fine art.

Each chapter opens with an original essay from a leading thinker whose work has helped shape public understanding of the contemporary world. The essays are followed by curated photographic narratives that move between global systems and individual lived experience, creating a layered portrait of the contemporary era.
Jon Lee Anderson — Staff Writer, The New Yorker
Mark Danner — Journalist & Author, UC Berkeley Graduate School of Journalism
Joia Mukherjee — Professor of Global Health, Harvard Medical School
Elisa Massimino — Human Rights Lawyer & Scholar, Georgetown
Nikhil Pal Singh — Chair of Social & Cultural Analysis, NYU
Lizabeth Cohen — Professor of American Studies, Harvard
David Kilcullen — Author, strategist, and former counterinsurgency advisor
Fred Turner — Professor of Communication, Stanford University
Richard Alley — Professor of Geosciences, Penn State University

Conceived by Editorial Director Joshua Herman and developed in collaboration with Creative & Visual Director Marc Asnin, the publication seeks to create a sweeping visual and intellectual portrait of a century still unfolding.

Rather than functioning solely as a photography anthology, Act One is structured as an interdisciplinary cultural work — pairing visual storytelling with historical analysis, political thought, journalism, and contemporary scholarship. The project moves between global systems and individual lived experience, asking how photography can help us understand the complexity, contradictions, and emotional realities of the modern era.
The book’s inaugural exhibition will open at QCC Art Gallery in October 2026, with plans for a traveling exhibition to universities, museums, and cultural institutions thereafter.
